title: Bishop VS Rook!
summary: Offer the bishop, then use a checking deflection to clear the promotion rank.

nodes.question: How can the bishop help before the pawn advances?
nodes.explanation: White must prevent the rook from settling behind b6 or reaching the eighth rank with time to stop promotion.

branches.title: Block, answer the check, and divert the rook
commentary: Begin from the complete five-piece source board.
Bc4 offers the bishop while preparing Bb3 to block the rook’s view of the b-pawn.
Rb1 goes behind the pawn, attempting the familiar rook blockade.
Bb3 blocks the b-file while remaining near the white king.
Ra1+ checks the king along the a-file, trying to displace its support.
Ba2 interposes against the check and protects b1 along the a2–b1 diagonal.
Re1 is the source’s attempt to reroute to the back rank.
b7 threatens promotion, keeping the rook under time pressure.
Re8 controls b8 along the eighth rank and also watches the bishop’s checking square e6.
Be6+ offers the bishop with check against Kg4, drawing the rook away from the promotion rank if it captures.
Rxe6 accepts the source’s illustrated sacrifice and abandons the eighth rank.
b8=Q promotes safely. This exact queen-versus-rook position is winning for White; the selected branch stops at the checked conversion.
branches.explanation: b8=Q promotes safely. This exact queen-versus-rook position is winning for White; the selected branch stops at the checked conversion.

branches.title: Take the bishop immediately
commentary: Compare the source’s immediate acceptance of the bishop sacrifice.
Bc4 offers material to gain promotion time.
Rxc4 captures, but places the rook where a timely blockade is difficult.
b7 reaches the seventh rank. Ka3 controls b4 and b3, while the pawn controls a8 and c8. The exact position is a checked White win.
branches.explanation: b7 reaches the seventh rank. Ka3 controls b4 and b3, while the pawn controls a8 and c8. The exact position is a checked White win.

branches.title: Push the pawn before preparing the bishop
commentary: Compare the source’s immediate pawn push.
b7 gives away the forced win because the bishop has not prepared an effective answer to the rook’s rear blockade.
Rb1 stops promotion from behind. This exact position is drawn; an eventual rook sacrifice against the pawn can leave White with only a bishop.

exercises.prompt: Why offer Bc4 before advancing the pawn?
exercises.answer: It prepares Bb3 and Ba2 against the checking blockade. Taking the bishop immediately instead loses time against b7.

exercises.prompt: Why can Be6+ work even when Re8 attacks e6?
exercises.answer: The capture moves the rook off the promotion rank. White trades the bishop for the tempo needed to promote safely.

startContext: Begin from the complete five-piece opening diagram. The selected ...Re1/...Re8 defense is met by Be6+ and the illustrated rook capture. The early bishop capture and premature pawn advance are checked separately; no exhaustive list of rook defenses is claimed.
